subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Mars: The Red Planet's Past
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mars: The Red Planet's Past usable.

hook.text: Mars once had rivers, lakes, and a thick atmosphere. If life ever started there, evidence might still be buried in its rocks.

buildup.text: Rovers have found ancient riverbeds, clay minerals, and chemicals that form in water—signs of a habitable past.

discovery.text: Curiosity found organic molecules and seasonal methane spikes on Mars. Both could have biological or geological origins.

twist.text: Mars lost its magnetic field billions of years ago. Without it, the solar wind stripped its atmosphere and dried its surface.

climax.text: Perseverance is collecting rock samples for return to Earth. Those samples could contain the first proof of ancient Martian life.

punchline.text: Mars was once wet and warm. Its rocks might hold fossils of ancient life.

quiz.question: Why is the Perseverance rover collecting rock samples on Mars?
options: To return them to Earth where they can be tested for signs of ancient life
To build a permanent base for future human colonists
To study the current Martian atmosphere for oxygen production

details.summary: Mars once had rivers, lakes, and possibly an ocean — conditions potentially suitable for life 3-4 billion years ago. Evidence from rover missions reveals ancient clay minerals and water-carved channels. If life ever arose on Mars, it may have retreated underground as the surface became cold and dry.
details.whyItMatters: Mars is the most accessible place to search for past extraterrestrial life. Evidence of ancient water means conditions were habitable, and preserved biosignatures in Martian rocks could prove life existed beyond Earth.
takeaways: Mars had rivers, lakes, and possibly an ocean billions of years ago
Rovers have found clay minerals indicating long-term water
Life may have retreated underground as conditions worsened

faq.question: What happened to Mars's water?
faq.answer: Mars lost its magnetic field roughly 4 billion years ago, allowing solar wind to strip away the atmosphere. Without atmospheric pressure, liquid water evaporated into space. Some water remains frozen at the poles and underground, but the surface became too cold and thin-aired for liquid.

faq.question: Has any evidence of past life been found on Mars?
faq.answer: Not definitively. The Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have found organic molecules and conditions consistent with habitability, but no confirmed biosignatures. Perseverance is collecting samples for return to Earth, where advanced lab analysis may provide a conclusive answer.
